title: Roosevelt wins a fourth term

facts.text: On 7 November 1944, President Franklin D. Roosevelt won a fourth term, defeating Republican Thomas E. Dewey, the governor of New York.
Roosevelt won 432 electoral votes to Dewey's 99, carrying 36 of the 48 states.
He took about 25.6 million popular votes to Dewey's 22.0 million, or 53.4 percent to 45.9 percent.
It was the closest of Roosevelt's four presidential elections.
His new running mate was Senator Harry S. Truman of Missouri, chosen after party leaders turned against Vice President Henry A. Wallace.
Roosevelt had serious health problems in 1944, which he and his doctors kept from the public, and Republicans made his health a campaign issue.
To answer the whispers, on 21 October 1944 he toured New York City for four hours in an open car in pouring rain.
The election was held in the middle of the war, and millions of service members voted by absentee ballot under state laws and a federal war ballot passed by Congress.
Army Signal Corps film shot the next day, 8 November 1944, shows soldiers of the 95th Signal Company in Moyeuvre, France, parading behind a jeep carrying a sign that reads "Roosevelt Elected."
The same reel shows soldiers of the 95th Infantry Division near Metz gathered around a portable radio in their foxholes, and the Army's film notes call the soldiers' show of joy "very stagey."
Roosevelt is the only president ever elected four times.
He was sworn in on 20 January 1945 in a short wartime ceremony on the South Portico of the White House instead of at the Capitol.
Less than three months later, on 12 April 1945, he died of a cerebral hemorrhage at Warm Springs, Georgia, and Truman became president.
The 22nd Amendment, passed by Congress in 1947 and ratified on 27 February 1951, now limits presidents to two elected terms.

film.shot_notes: U.S. Army Signal Corps film, 8 November 1944 (silent per the shot card). The file is the stretch from 3:35 to 6:40 of the NARA reel, re-encoded at 30 fps. File times: 0:00 to 0:10 a jeep crosses a bridge in Moyeuvre, France; 0:10 to 1:10 soldiers of the 95th Signal Company parade and cheer behind a jeep carrying a sign reading 'Roosevelt Elected', with townspeople running alongside, the best moving opener (the sign is clearest at about 0:30 to 1:00); 1:15 slate LIB 522; 1:20 to 2:25 soldiers of the 95th Infantry Division near Metz gathered around a portable radio in a foxhole and at a jeep; 2:25 to 3:05 soldiers read election returns from a bulletin board on a town street. The shot card calls the soldiers' show of joy 'very stagey'.

video.hook: A day later, GIs in France paraded the news.

kit.youtubeDescription:
On 7 November 1944, President Franklin D. Roosevelt won a fourth term, defeating Thomas E. Dewey with 432 electoral votes to 99. It was the closest of his four presidential elections, held in the middle of the war, with millions of service members voting by absentee ballot. His new running mate was Senator Harry S. Truman. Roosevelt is the only president ever elected four times; less than three months after his inauguration he died at Warm Springs, Georgia.

This is real U.S. Army Signal Corps film shot the next day, 8 November 1944, in Moyeuvre, France: soldiers of the 95th Signal Company parade behind a jeep carrying a sign that reads "Roosevelt Elected." The Army's film notes call the soldiers' show of joy "very stagey." The original film is silent.
